title: Recognize hazards before work
objectives: Identify hazards and select a safe next action.
explanation: A hazard is a source of possible harm; risk considers how harm could occur and its consequences. Before work, look for damaged cables, wet areas, unstable access, falling objects, traffic, heavy loads and blocked exits. A neat-looking site can still contain hidden services or energized equipment.

Prefer eliminating a hazard or changing the method before relying only on personal protective equipment. A beginner should report an unsafe condition and stay outside the danger area. Do not start an unfamiliar task because a customer says it is urgent. This awareness course does not replace the employer’s risk assessment, task training, supervision or site-specific controls.
example: A loose cable crosses a busy walkway. The exercise asks for a controlled routing solution and communication, not merely a warning shouted once.
exercise: Identify three hazards in a fictional storeroom and propose one safer alternative for each.
model_response: Blocked exit: clear through authorized action. Unstable stack: isolate and request safe restacking. Damaged lead: keep out of service and report.
key_points: Look for the mechanism of harm
Pause when safe controls are missing
